「ン」で置くより、hold the sound――英語は「伸ばし」のつもりで発音すると何が変わるか

Maybe English final consonants, especially /n/, become easier when you stop appending a Japanese-style 「ン」 and instead think of holding an articulatory state. The idea is useful, but only after one correction: this is not a rule to make English sounds longer. Japanese word-final nasals can in fact be relatively longer than English ones. The practical shift is from adding a mora to sustaining the consonant gesture without inserting an extra vowel or dropping the articulation too early.
